ARHC's mission is to improve health outcomes and contribute to SDG 3 by providing tailored solutions and advisory services. Its expertise encompasses programme and fund management, pharmaceuticals and health sector procurement, and technical expertise in the health sector. ARHC also extends its capabilities and services to UNOPS multi-country and country offices in the region, promoting regional collaboration and impact in the health sector. Role Purpose The Programme Manager provides strategic, technical, and operational leadership for the planning, implementation, monitoring, and performance management of Global Fund-supported programmes, ensuring the achievement of results within approved scope, time, budget, quality, and risk parameters. The role oversees the full programme lifecycle, coordinates multidisciplinary teams and key stakeholders including National Programmes, Sub-Recipients, donors, and other partners, and ensures compliance with UNOPS policies, Global Fund requirements, and national strategies. The Programme Manager is responsible for programme performance, financial and operational planning, risk management, monitoring and reporting, while promoting evidence-based decision-making, continuous improvement, institutional capacity strengthening, and the sustainability and accountability of programme results. Functions / Key Results Expected Programme Delivery and Performance The Programme Manager is responsible for the effective management and delivery of one or more Global Fund-supported programmes, ensuring implementation is aligned with approved Grant Agreements, national strategic priorities, donor requirements and UNOPS policies. Coordinate implementation across Sub-Recipients (SRs), National Programmes and technical partners to ensure activities remain aligned with approved workplans, budgets and performance frameworks. Monitor programme implementation against scope, schedule, budget, quality and risk parameters, utilising real-time digital dashboards and advanced data analytics to proactively identify implementation challenges and recommend timely corrective actions. Lead grant-making, reprogramming and grant closure processes, ensuring alignment with Global Fund guidance and country priorities. Review annual work plans, implementation plans, budgets and operational documents submitted by SRs and National Programmes, ensuring technical quality, feasibility and compliance with donor requirements. Coordinate programme implementation with cross-functional teams including Finance, Procurement, Supply Chain Management (PSM), Monitoring and Evaluation, Human Resources and Compliance to ensure integrated programme delivery. Promote gender equality, equity, community engagement, safeguarding, environmental sustainability and human rights principles throughout programme implementation. Identify opportunities for programme innovation, operational efficiencies and continuous improvement to strengthen programme performance and maximize impact. Financial, Grant and Procurement Management The Programme Manager supports effective financial and grant management throughout the programme lifecycle. Key responsibilities include: Lead annual planning, budgeting and forecasting processes. Monitor programme expenditures, commitments and burn rates against approved budgets. Review financial reports and expenditure trends to identify implementation risks and recommend mitigation measures. Support preparation of cash forecasts and disbursement planning. Coordinate grant revisions, budget reallocations and portfolio optimization exercises. Work closely with Procurement and Supply Management teams on forecasting, quantification and procurement planning for health products and programme commodities. Contribute to preparation of Terms of Reference, technical specifications, bid evaluations and contract management where applicable. Support internal and external audits and ensure implementation of agreed audit recommendations. Stakeholder Engagement and Partnership Management The Programme Manager plays a key coordination role between UNOPS and national and international stakeholders. Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between PR units, SRs and technical partners. Support stakeholder consultations during grant making, implementation, grant-making and reprogramming processes. Promote knowledge sharing and dissemination of programme achievements, lessons learned and best practices. Programme Monitoring, Reporting and Quality Assurance The Programme Manager ensures effective monitoring of programme performance and compliance with donor requirements. Responsibilities include: Monitor programme implementation against agreed indicators, milestones and deliverables. Review programme performance data and work closely with the Monitoring and Evaluation team to identify implementation gaps, risks and opportunities for improvement. Ensure timely preparation and submission of quality Progress Updates (PUDRs), management reports, donor reports and other programme deliverables. Support programme performance reviews, grant rating assessments and portfolio reviews. Coordinate routine implementation reviews, field monitoring missions and supportive supervision visits. Ensure compliance with Global Fund policies, UNOPS procedures and national programme requirements. Promote data quality, accountability and evidence-based decision-making across programme implementation. Support implementation of recommendations arising from audits, Local Fund Agent (LFA) reviews, technical assistance missions and programme evaluations. Technical Leadership and Capacity Development The Programme Manager provides technical and operational leadership to strengthen programme implementation. The incumbent will: Provide technical and project management guidance to National Programmes, SRs and implementing partners on programme implementation, grant requirements and operational planning. Support development and revision of implementation guidelines, operational tools and standard operating procedures. Identify institutional and technical capacity gaps and coordinate appropriate capacity strengthening initiatives. Organize and facilitate workshops, technical meetings and learning events. Mentor programme personnel and contribute to strengthening programme management capacity across partners. Promote organizational learning by documenting lessons learned, innovations and good practices. Contribute to the standardization, to the extent possible, of NP, SRs, and IPs programme management capacity development efforts across the programmes. Digitization, Data Governance and Analytics Support the M&E function in the development, implementation and continuous improvement of databases, electronic information systems, digital health platforms and other technology-enabled tools used by UNOPS and implementing partners. Support the development and maintenance of real-time digital dashboards, automated reporting tools and interactive data visualizations to monitor programme performance, identify emerging trends and provide timely information for management decision-making, in coordination with M&E functions. Assess existing and proposed digital tools and system enhancements, identify opportunities for automation and improved analytics, and recommend fit-for-purpose, sustainable and cost-effective solutions. Personnel Management The Programme Manager will: Supervise Programme Officers, Associates and other assigned personnel. Manage staff performance, development and coaching in accordance with UNOPS policies. Foster an inclusive, respectful and collaborative working environment. Promote staff wellbeing, diversity, inclusion and safeguarding. Ensure compliance with UNDSS security requirements and organizational duty of care responsibilities. Knowledge Management and Continuous Improvement The Programme Manager contributes to organizational excellence through: Developing programme briefs, analytical reports, briefing notes and presentations for senior management, donors and other stakeholders. Supporting strategic planning, portfolio analysis and resource mobilization efforts. Documenting lessons learned and contributing to Communities of Practice and organizational knowledge-sharing initiatives. Driving the creation of digital knowledge repositories to document and disseminate best practices across integrated public health programming. Monitoring developments in global health financing, Global Fund policies and disease programme strategies to inform programme implementation. Identifying opportunities to strengthen programme effectiveness, operational efficiency and sustainability. Proficiency in project management tools for tracking deliverables, timelines, and resource allocation across integrated health portfolios. Desired Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country is desired. Experience in development or humanitarian contexts is desired. Familiarity with Power BI or Tableau to track and present high-level portfolio progress and operational bottlenecks to stakeholders. Advanced use of enterprise collaboration tools to manage cross-functional communication and document control.
